metadata.scenario_context: A group of software engineers working remotely for a global tech company decides to initiate a team-building meeting early in January. Luis raises the idea of going on a strike to protest against some changes from the company's management.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from Spain strongly disagree they would never join strikes.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Nicaragua strongly agree they would never join strikes.

agent_1.goal_1: Suggest the possibility of scheduling the team-building meeting on January 1st.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether it is common to discuss or join strikes as a form of protest.

agent_2.goal_1: Discuss a specific date for the team-building meeting.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether it is common to join strikes as a form of protest.

shared_prefix.speaker: Javier
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Ahmed, what do you think about scheduling the team-building meeting on January 1st? It could be a fresh start for the year. 

Also, I've been thinking... is it common for software engineers to discuss or join strikes as a method of protest? It feels a bit unusual to me.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Ahmed
shared_prefix.message:
January 1st... hmm, that might be tough for a lot of people. Maybe we should look at another date, like the first full week of January? 

As for strikes, I think it's quite uncommon for us. In Nicaragua, we generally wouldn’t join strikes. We prefer to find other ways to address issues. It's just not part of our culture.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Javier
shared_prefix.message:
I get that January 1st might be challenging. We could definitely consider another date... but I still think starting the year with a team-building event could set a positive tone.
